correctness.rationale: For every fixed R>1, the product of independent failure probabilities gives P(K>n)=exp(c-c R^n), c=aR/(R-1). Summation by parts produces an exactly convergent expected-size series. Its bilateral extension omits at most c/(R-1), and uniform convergence yields an O_R(a) remainder. A change of variables computes Fourier coefficients as Gamma(1+2 pi i k/log R)/log R, nonzero by the Gamma reciprocal Euler product. Fixed logarithmic phase sequences attain every value of the continuous nonconstant periodic function. The full argument is in RESULT.md; 276 diagnostics passed from the package check.py, which does not substitute for proof.

originality.rationale: Closest early-detection works derive exact finite-round probabilities, continuous-survey approximations, or optimized effort, without an identified nonzero logarithmic-phase correction, uniform fixed-phase weak-sensitivity limit interval, or Gamma Fourier spectrum. The fixed-phase limiting phenomenon is not a mere rephrasing of the continuous-time rule of thumb, although the finite detection law and the Mellin technique are prior art. Historical priority is provisional: a plausible 2012 first-discovery paper was available only as abstract and a relevant 2025/2026 article only as partial text.
residual_risks: The full 2012 original first-discovery paper might contain an equivalent logarithmic-phase asymptotic or a stronger representation.
The later 2025/2026 invasion size-at-detection full text was not accessible and may treat periodic survey calendars.
More general Mellin-asymptotic literature might imply the mathematical phenomenon in a wider geometric-lattice framework, though this ecological fixed-phase consequence was not located.
Biological unbounded exponential growth becomes unrealistic at the large population sizes required by the limit.

value.rationale: Periodic ecological surveys and size-dependent detection are directly motivated by published early-invasion models. The theorem provides a mathematically sharp and reproducible limitation of phase-averaged continuous-survey approximations: the weak-sensitivity expected discovery burden has a nondegenerate limit interval, an exact average, and an all-R nonzero Gamma harmonic. At R=10 two attainable phases differ by about 0.578 in sensitivity-scaled expected size. This is a structural bound, not a small routine table entry; the infinite-growth assumption sharply limits practical extrapolation.
